result.topic_en: Riemann determines a constant factor in a theta-function quotient identity by setting variables equal, and argues that the vanishing of a theta function at certain half-period-type arguments implies the simultaneous vanishing of its partial derivatives up to some order at $v_\nu = r_\nu$.

methods.what: Determining a rational factor by specializing variables (setting $\mathfrak{z}_1=z_1$, $\sigma_1=\mathfrak{s}_1$) and taking the square root
Identity for a quotient of products of theta functions in terms of sums of first derivatives times the abelian differentials $\varphi_\nu$

Inductive argument: identical vanishing of theta at sums of m abelian integrals implies vanishing of derivatives of order n at sums of m−n integrals, hence all derivatives up to order m vanish at $v_\nu=r_\nu$
